html:
A group of food plants that Native Americans of the eastern woodlands of North America tamed on their own, one of about ten places in the world where farming began independently. Gathering of these seed plants grew into real cultivation over thousands of years, and by about 1800 BCE several species were being grown.

The crops included:

  • sunflower and sumpweed, grown for oily seeds
  • a native squash, used for seeds and as containers
  • goosefoot (chenopod), erect knotweed, maygrass and little barley, grown for starchy seeds

These crops fed the mound building peoples of the Adena and Hopewell cultures. Later, maize came north from Mexico and slowly took over, and by about 900 CE it fed the towns of Cahokia and the Mississippian world. Most of the old seed crops were then dropped. Only the sunflower and squash are still grown widely today.
